content.text: Section 20 is complete and Section 21.3 expressly excludes indemnification obligations from the liability cap. This satisfies the preferred position, so no redline is needed.

input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets and exceeds the preferred position. 20.1 gives a Vendor defend/indemnify/hold-harmless obligation covering Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims relating to the Services or Deliverables, with no customer-modification/combination/specification carve-outs. 20.2 adds the remaining preferred triggers: Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (plus bodily injury/property damage). 20.4 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice with a material-prejudice qualifier, cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense, control of defence, and no adverse settlement without consent). 20.5 provides the infringement remedies (procure, modify/replace, or terminate and refund) expressly "in addition to" the defence obligation, and bars Vendor from terminating unaffected Services. The Customer-side indemnity in 20.3 is appropriately narrow — limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used strictly as authorized and Customer's violation of Applicable Law — with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions. Direction is correct: the substantive burden falls on Vendor. Liability treatment also favours us: Section 21.3 defines "Excluded Claims" to include a Party's indemnification obligations, IP infringement, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud, so Vendor's indemnity sits outside the 21.1 cap entirely — better than the fallback's 3x super-cap. Section 19.4 and 19.5 further confirm no warranty remedy or disclaimer limits the indemnities. No redline required.
